sentences.text: The name Camptosaurus translates to 'flexible lizard', a title taken from Greek roots meaning 'bent' and 'lizard'.
This herbivorous ornithischian dinosaur, which possessed a beak, typically measured between five and six meters long and weighed from 500 to 1000 kilograms.
Its jaw held teeth that were packed more tightly together than those found in other euornithopods from the same geological formation.
The animal had a stocky build supported by strong hind legs and large feet equipped with four toes.
A preserved embryo measuring roughly 23 centimeters in length was discovered within the Morrison Formation at the Dinosaur National Monument in Utah.
John Foster, a museum curator, observed that the creature featured distinct crests along its sides and small tooth-like projections on its edges.
Remains of a small euornithopod were located by William Harlow Reed in Albany County, Wyoming, on the fourth day of September in 1879.
Professor Othniel Charles Marsh initially named the find Camptonotus, but he later changed the genus name in 1885 because that name was already taken by a cricket.
Marsh designated C. dispar as the type species using fossils from Quarry 13 near Como Bluff, while C. amplus was named based on a foot found by Arthur Lakes at Quarry 1A.
Heavy wear patterns on the teeth suggest the dinosaur consumed vegetation that was relatively tough to chew.
Researchers estimate that Camptosaurus could run at speeds of 25 kilometers per hour by comparing it to other iguanodontians.
It shared its environment with theropods such as Allosaurus and Ceratosaurus, as well as sauropods like Apatosaurus and Diplodocus.
In the deepest layers of the quarry, the only predatory dinosaur found was the small Coelurus, which likely did not threaten adult Camptosaurus.
Marsh originally placed the genus in its own family, Camptosauridae, during 1885.
Some researchers have alternatively classified it as an early member of Iguanodontidae, though this placement remains a subject of ongoing debate.
Current phylogenetic analysis defines Camptosaurus as a basal member of the clade Ankylopollexia.
Specimens of C. dispar from Quarry 13 are dated to the Callovian-Oxfordian stages of the Late Jurassic.
The species lived approximately between 160 and 145 million years ago across what is now western North America.
Three species of this dinosaur have been identified within the Morrison Formation across Colorado, Oklahoma, Utah, and Wyoming.
There is disagreement regarding whether C. prestwichii should remain in Camptosaurus or be moved to the separate genus Cumnoria due to closer relations with advanced iguanodonts.
An analysis indicates that C. aphanoecetes is more closely related to advanced iguanodonts, leading to its reclassification as Uteodon.
Because of the distinct status of Uteodon, it has become difficult to determine exactly which Morrison material belongs to Camptosaurus.
Krumenacker et al. (2026) described three iguanodontian specimens from the Simon Quarry in Wyoming that show a morphology different from Dryosaurus and Camptosaurus.
